rationale:
The subject has two obligations. `dependencies()` must return a snapshot of the observations collected so far. Later reads must still contribute to the same execution. `snapshots_record_exact_reads_and_retain_distinct_versions` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs` covers both, and its `{test}` marker for the subject is present.

- **Snapshot of what has been collected so far:**
  - A fresh `ValidationContext::new` returns an empty list from `dependencies()`, so nothing is reported before any read.
  - After `read(&1)`, the test takes `earlier = inspection.dependencies()`.
  - The test then reads again after the graph content changes to "after". It asserts `earlier == [Dependency::Node(1, fp("before"))]`.
  - This shows the returned value is a detached snapshot. It was not mutated by later reads, and it reports exactly the reads made before the call.
- **Later reads continue to contribute:**
  - After the second read of node 1 ("after"), `inspection.dependencies()` equals `[Node(1, before), Node(1, after)]`. The context kept accumulating after the earlier snapshot was taken.
  - The failed `read(&2)` adds no dependency, which the same assertion confirms.
  - `finish` then yields a record whose `dependencies` match the same list, so the accumulated state persists to the end of the execution.

A fake implementation could return an empty list, return a live view, or stop recording after the first call. The assertions above reject each of these.

`public_exports_match_the_appendix` in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs` only checks the export inventory. It adds nothing to this requirement, and the requirement needs nothing from it.

I found no untested obligation and no gap.

text: Return a snapshot of the observations collected so far. Later reads continue to contribute to this execution.
